title: Concurrent cache writers cannot expose a partial entry
question: With two processes writing the same cache key concurrently, can any reader observe a partial entry? PASS requires atomic publish and a well-defined winner; readers must see either the old entry or a complete new one.

cache_layer.mutant_publish: in-place overwrite with a visible truncated window
cache_layer.note: Production Cache.put (platform/plugin/cache.py) is content-addressed via hash_bytes, so two distinct payloads cannot share a key. The catalog question is named-key concurrent publish; the measured layer is probes/TST-0174/atomic_cache.py (tmp+os.replace, same pattern as platform/plugin/fsops.py atomic_write_bytes).

reviewer.notes: Probe 2 is a mechanically different measurement: it removes atomic publish and requires partial reads, then scans for leftover tmp files on the atomic path.

tests.name: property test: 1,000 interleavings with a reader asserting integrity on every read
mutation control: remove the atomic publish and confirm partial reads appear
(b) inspection for leftover temp files after concurrent atomic publish
(a) reader-side integrity checks across the concurrent run

negative_controls.description: Atomic os.replace: zero partial reads across 1000 dual-writer trials. In-place overwrite: the same reader must observe at least one truncated or checksum-invalid entry.

evidence.claim: Two processes publishing the same key via tmp+os.replace never expose a partial entry; every reader observation is a complete old or complete new payload, and the post-join winner is A or B.
